items.title: 68088_Wilbur B. Ware, Sr oral history interview

ctx.x: But I said, "Okay, I'll go." He didn't really have to twist my arm too much. I wanted to see what Newport was like. I hadn't been up there since the riot. Anyway, we took off that night. We got to Newport the next afternoon and they had us sandwiched in. He had Howard Johnson on tuba. He had Grachan Moncur on trombone, himself on tenor, and he had a poet, crazy guy, Leon Bibbs (PHONETIC) -- not Leon Bibbs, but --
Leroy Bibbs. He's nuts. He was in the same vein, you might say, Lenny Bruce and all the cats like that, which you would call -- I won't say beat poet, a hippie
